cards.about: Justin describes the Sunday gathering of the Christians.
cards.author: Justin Martyr
cards.excerpt: And on the day called Sunday, all who live in cities or in the country gather together to one place, and the memoirs of the apostles or the writings of the prophets are read, as long as time permits

cards.about: Pliny reports what the Christians he questioned said they did.
cards.author: Pliny the Younger
cards.reference: Letters 10.96, as translated in the note to Eusebius, Church History 3.33
cards.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 1 (1890)
cards.excerpt: they had been accustomed to come together on a fixed day before daylight and to sing responsively a song unto Christ as God; and to bind themselves with an oath, not with a view to the commission of some crime, but, on the contrary, that they would not commit theft, nor robbery, nor adultery, that they would not break faith, nor refuse to restore a deposit when asked for it.

cards.about: Eusebius gives Trajan's answer in a line.
cards.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
cards.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 1 (1890)
cards.excerpt: that the race of Christians should not be sought after, but when found should be punished

cards.about: Dionysius of Alexandria on the Christians who nursed the sick in the plague.
cards.author: Dionysius of Alexandria
cards.work: Letter on the plague, kept in Eusebius, Church History
cards.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 1 (1890)
cards.excerpt: The most of our brethren were unsparing in their exceeding love and brotherly kindness. They held fast to each other and visited the sick fearlessly, and ministered to them continually, serving them in Christ.

cards.about: The bishop of Rome counts the people his church was feeding.
cards.author: Cornelius of Rome
cards.work: Letter to Fabius of Antioch, kept in Eusebius, Church History
cards.translation: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 1 (1890)
cards.excerpt: over fifteen hundred widows and persons in distress, all of whom the grace and kindness of the Master nourish

cards.about: Polycarp's answer when the proconsul told him to reproach Christ.
cards.author: The church at Smyrna
cards.excerpt: Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury: how then can I blaspheme my King and my Saviour?

cards.about: Perpetua's own account of what she told her father.
cards.author: Perpetua
cards.work: The Passion of the Holy Martyrs Perpetua and Felicitas
cards.excerpt: Neither can I call myself anything else than what I am, a Christian.

cards.author: Tertullian
cards.excerpt: The oftener we are mown down by you, the more in number we grow; the blood of Christians is seed.

cards.about: Cyprian, writing once the persecution had passed, on how quickly many gave way.
cards.author: Cyprian of Carthage
cards.excerpt: They indeed did not wait to be apprehended ere they ascended, or to be interrogated ere they denied. Many were conquered before the battle, prostrated before the attack.

cards.about: The unknown writer's description of the Christians.
cards.author: Unknown
cards.excerpt: They dwell in their own countries, but simply as sojourners. As citizens, they share in all things with others, and yet endure all things as if foreigners. Every foreign land is to them as their native country, and every land of their birth as a land of strangers.
